cards.note: These palms where the crown has been cut, are very often found near Aracataca and some smaller towns North of it.
In general, banana plantation can be found mostly in Quindio and Magdalena, sometimes in Northwest-Antioquia and Cordoba, and rarely in surrounding provinces of Quindio.

Large amounts of banana plants in plantations are commonly found in different areas.

Paired with Cloudy Gen 3 Coverage, they're most common in Northwestern Antioquia.
In Magdalena you will often see banana plantations in a dry sandy/dirty area with mountains to your east.
In Quindio you will commonly find banana plantations behind hedges.

cards.a: Agriculture - Banana - Small Field / No Hedge
cards.note: In the states surrounding Quindio you will find smaller banana plantations along the road not behind hedges.

The coffee belt stretches in the valley between Medellin and Cali. In the North, you will only find it near the Venezuelan border.

Olives and Tea have a very similar distribution.
Common Guava mostly appears in the valley between the western and the central mountain range in Colombia, but it can also appear in other valleys.
Guadua Bamboo plantations are found mainly in Caldas, but also in the adjecent Tolima, Quindio and Risaralda.
Oilpalms can be found mainly in Meta and Casanare. They are also very common around the 45 near Fundacion and Aracataca. Sometimes, you can find them in Barrancabermeja.
Sugarcane will mainly be found in Cauca and Valle de Cauca.
Bright Colored Houses & Unique Pavement.
Houses with roofs like this are commonly found along the coast, especially near Cartagena and Barranquilla.

cards.a: Car Meta - Gen 3 - white/blue striped car
cards.note: Gen 3 with the white-blue car follows a straight line between Cartagena and Medellín, has partial coverage along Route 80 west of Bosconia, as well as along Route 45 north of Bucaramanga and east of Medellín.

Gen 4 coverage with the grey car is not found north of Montería, has a gap between Bucaramanga and Bogotá, forms a 'staircase' pattern with right angles at Medellín and Bogotá, covers areas around Bucaramanga, and has a missing section around Popayán.
Gen 4 with the white car has no coverage south of Cali, very little around Medellín, and forms a curved pattern around Medellín.

This unique vehicle can be found in and around Leticia, the Southernmost town in Colombia.

NOTE: The long concrete blocks seen in the bottom left corner are a reliable way of recognising the road North of Leticia.
The island of Providencia, located roughly 90 kilometres North of San Andrés, is home to this unique grey truck.
Coverage on the Caribbean island of San Andrés was taken by this distinct white car.
A camera glitch that makes a part of the image look very saturated can be found in southern Colombia.

On the road in Arauca and in the city of Arauca in northeastern Colombia, there is virtually only cloudy, bad weather coverage. Furthermore, there was a small camera glitch where you can see this small rift northeast of the driving direction.
A Second Google Car is visible in many random spots. The most prominent spots are the 26 in Cauca, Vda. Chontaduro (near Popoyan) and the road between Pital and Tarqui.

cards.a: Coverage Meta - Double Google Car - Aguachica
cards.note: This instance of a second google car can be seen on Carrera 4, an offroad of the 45 near Aguachica.

cards.a: Coverage Meta - Double Google Car - Villavicencio
cards.note: This instance of a second google car can be seen on the east-west road, directly south of Guayuriba River, which is south of Villavicencio.
Large lake, mostly winter coverage. A small stretch also has summer coverage.
If you see rainy coverage, combined with strong fog, you're on the 64.
This combination can be found on the 65 in Caqueta and the 45 in Putumayo.
Rainy coverage with very orange-brown soil can be found on this road to La Florida.
Rainy coverage is most common on the highways 20, 24, 50 and 64.
If you see a lake, paired with an overexposed Gen 4 camera, you're probably on this lake south of Sogamoso.
This stick on the camera can be found between El Guio and El Boral (near the Cundinamarca-Meta border near Villavicencio)

cards.a: Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Arauca
cards.note: On this road, you can see a sunset through the clouds. It's not always easy to recognize, however.

cards.a: Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Hato Corozal
cards.note: On this road, you can see a slight sunset through the clouds. It is pretty flat, with mountains in the Northwest.
This unique cobblestone pavement is found is the historic town of Barichara, Santander.
In Barranquilla, you can often find this bollard with roadnames on intersections.
The stretch of the 40 to Buenaventura is an important route for trucks, so if you see many trucks, it's worth a thought.
orange & blue
Yellow with dark numbers
Green paint with yellow numbers

Usually pretty tall with oval windows, circle windows might not be as trustworthy.

Very common as there are few plastic counters in this region.
This european-style (specifically spanish style bollard) is found in Cundinamarca, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.
H-shaped lamp attachment plates can be found in Bogota.
Orange paint with black numbers

This red lamp style is unique to Tolima province.

Note by MB: I only found it in Ibague, not in any other towns in Tolima. Also, the meta is more about the color and the shape of the lamp, not about the arrangement of the lights.
Green or yellow, modern bus. Often on a dedicated bus lane. Found in Pereira metropolitan area.

These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.
Found in Barranquilla and Santa Marta
Rectangular lamp attachment plates can be found mainly in Medellin, sometimes further North, especially in Monteria and Cucuta.
Yellow paint with red numbers. Found all over Risaralda and the towns of Istmina and Quibdo in Choco.
Asymmetrical poles with a "Sarawak" extension (a vertical stalk coming out the top), can often be found East of Andes. Note that this pole is not 100%, and has been spotted elsewhere.
These spikes can be found on the 40 and the 62.
The uniquely shaped supporting metal piece can be found in Barranquilla. (Similar to the Providencia design)
Providencia street lights are green and supported by a trapezoidal sheet of metal underneath. (The metal sheet without a green lamp can also be found in Barranquilla)
This red bus drives in the town (not the country) Armenia.
Orange tag with white numbers
TransLogo vans are common throughtout Boyaca Department. You will most often see them on the routes Tunja-Sogamoso and Tunja-Duitama.
White Transmetro buses can be found in Barranquilla.
If you see many puddles and a pavement out of '+' shaped stones, you're in Tumaco.
If you see these poletops you will find yourself in Valle Del Cauca.
Yellow, with black numbers. Several digits can be in one row.
If you see a bike lane, and get East of Andes vibes, you're most likely on the road through Los Tobitos to Villavicencio.

cards.a: Landscape - Deep grey & stony soil in Gen 3
cards.note: This type of soil can be found in towns near the pacific coast.

East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.

Since it's to the east of the Andes, you may see mountains in the west, but never in the east.
This striking cone-shaped mountain can often be seen from the surrounding area of Guatape.
The only road in Guaviare goes from to Guaviare (city), and continues south up until Vda. El Trueno. It can be recognized by the orange-looking dust on the road.
This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.
The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.
This road leading from the 65 to the town of Orocue is characterized by its unique angle and the orange/brown dirt.

Paramos refers to alpine tundra ecosystems located in the mountains. These kinds of regions are easy to guess by how little vegetation grows here. The best clue is these odd looking pants. ( giant rosette plants ).

Note by MB: In my experience, this appears most commonly south of Bogota, still in the capital district.

In southern Colombia, around the city of Pasto, there are hilly fields that are unique in that they are bordered by hedges. The hedges are very thick and form very distinctive lines on the hills. It almost gives off a “British” vibe. If you are sure that it is Colombia, this is a very good meta, but such fields with hedges also occur in Ecuador.

!! In very rare cases, such hedges on hills can also occur in other parts of Colombia. !!
Santa Rosalia is the only town covered in Vichada. So if you see red/orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 loc, you should go there.
If you see a swamp road with extremely sunny coverage, you're probably on the 74 in Sucre.
The 74, the 78 and a few other roads more north have very swampy parts, you can see on the map where these are by zooming.

cards.a: Landscape - Unique Road - 78 west of Pailitas
cards.note: This road is characterised by low clouds and a towering mountain in the east.

You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.

NOTE: In the older Generation 3 coverage, you will also see tall mountains in the distance.

cards.a: Landscape - Unique Road - Uribia to Puerto Boliviar
cards.note: You can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of La Guajira landscape (extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti), the straightness and the train track always present to the East.
Vichada is characterize by hazy Gen 4 coverage and Red Dirt.
As a result of slave trade, the Pacific coast of Colombia is home to an overwhelming majority of Afro-Colombians.
This trekker can be recognized by the unique pavement and houses.
Cacti are most commonly found in the North near Valledupar. Sometimes they can appear in Huila, too.
This tree is found mainly around Medellin, but it has been spotted in other random spots.
The Kapok tree can be found throughout Colombia, but is most common between the central and eastern mountain range.
This palm is found in mountainous regions of Colombia, mainly in Quindio, as the name suggests.

In Colombia you will most commonly find these trees that appear to have a knot on top of their trunk in the dark red areas. The province of Cordoba has the most gen 4 out of the others so if you see these in gen 4 consider Cordoba. (If the area is flat/semi hilly, You can find these trees in the mountains aswell everywhere)
These wide trees, usually near fences, are found in Northern regions, especially near Monteria and Sincelejo.
